flightPlan.confirmStart: Start the planned flight? No tasting records will be created yet.
flightPlan.description: A proposal stores bottle references, not tasting records.
flightPlan.excludedAvailability: Additional matching bottlings excluded by availability: {excludedAvailability}. Check “Eligible bottles”.
flightPlan.excludedScope: Additional matching bottlings outside the filtered collection: {excludedScope}.
flightPlan.help.balanced.details: Automatic settings add 4 × weighted cask-family coverage K, up to 1 point for known feature differences within shared families (4 × J), and 2 per age class Q, plus user preferences (Pref). Missing information does not count as distinct diversity.
flightPlan.help.balanced.text: Prefers varied aroma families, moderate intensity gaps, and a spread of known cask families and age classes. Unrecognized cask notes or missing ages are not guessed.
flightPlan.help.balanced.title: Balanced
flightPlan.help.basics.distanceDetails: dG(A,B) is the mean absolute difference across shared rated radar axes divided by 10 (0–1). At least two shared axes are required; otherwise the flavor distance is unknown, not zero. Balanced and the sequence search still use the unnormalized distance (0–10).
flightPlan.help.basics.example: Example: Smoky 7/8, Peaty 8/7 and Fruity 2/3 give raw distance 1 and dG = 0.1.
flightPlan.help.basics.intensityDetails: ABV is the alcohol percentage; if unavailable, 40 is used. The profile mean includes assessed axes only (no profile: 0). Smoky and peaty each contribute one quarter of their assessed score again. This is not measured sensory intensity.
flightPlan.help.basics.noveltyDetails: Never tasted: 30 points; no assessed radar profile: 4; open bottle: 3. A valid last-tasted date adds about one point per 30 elapsed days, capped at 10. Without a date this part is zero.
flightPlan.help.basics.title: Definitions and calculations
flightPlan.help.basics.unfamiliarDetails: U is the minimum comparable profile distance to the tasting history of other bottlings (including external tastings). When no comparable record exists, U = 0. Unknown flavors are never guessed as novel.
flightPlan.help.candidates: Eligible bottles are non-empty physical bottles according to availability and any active collection filters. Only one bottle per bottling is selected (open first, then samples). The planner scores whole groups, tries multiple starting bottles and improves candidates through swaps. A globally optimal selection is not guaranteed. By default, only open bottles are considered. When particular cask or age criteria are set, the proposal also shows matches and matching bottlings excluded by availability or collection filters.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.classification: The free-text cask description is interpreted as cask families and recognizable features without changing collection data. Sherry, Port, Madeira and Wine are separate families; Wine here means non-fortified wine. Rum has no additional subtypes. Other contains explicitly recognized other casks; Unknown means unclassifiable descriptions.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.coverage: Explicit finishes have weight 0.5; other descriptions have weight 1. Without a phase description the phase remains unknown. The maturation filter includes such casks, while the finish filter requires an explicit finish. This does not establish full maturation. Automatic cask diversity counts at most one unit per bottle, spread across its families; each family contributes at most one unit. Known subtypes refine the comparison by at most 25% of the remaining distance. Missing or overlapping features are not independent diversity signals. This is not a sensory score.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.examples: Examples: Oloroso, PX and Fino for a Sherry comparison; Ruby and Tawny for Port; Sercial, Verdelho, Bual and Malvasia for Madeira; Bourbon, Rum and Wine for a cask comparison. Colheita also matches Tawny; Sauternes matches both white wine and sweet wine. A bourbon-matured whisky with an Oloroso finish matches Sherry + Finish, not Sherry + Maturation. Without strict filters, matches are preferred; with strict filters, nonmatches are excluded. Selecting several families does not guarantee that each will be represented in the flight.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.missing: Keyword classification is not a verified cask history. Specific filters require recognizable evidence; unknown subtypes do not match specific subtype selections; unspecified phases qualify for maturation, not finish. Age is not a quality rating and affects the tasting order only slightly. Missing maturation or flavor data are not invented.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.selection: Choose “Prefer particular cask types” to select multiple families. Selected families can be refined in individual expandable sections. The selected feature count and a summary remain visible. “Reset” clears cask preferences including the maturation phase. Selecting none allows all families. Without a subtype, every bottling in the family qualifies, including those with unknown subtypes. Multiple families or values within one dimension are alternatives (OR). Different dimensions within a family and the selected phase must match the same cask (AND). Unknown subtypes do not satisfy a specific refinement. Even with soft preferences, the cask family bonus requires the selected maturation phase.
flightPlan.help.caskAge.title: Cask type and age: classification and options
flightPlan.help.contrast.details: Adds 2.5 times the weighted pair differences. The default sign is +1; similar cask or similar age reverses its own component. Missing radar comparisons incur −14.
flightPlan.help.contrast.text: Prefers contrasts in aroma, cask type and age while limiting very large intensity jumps. An explicit cask/age preference can reverse individual components.
flightPlan.help.contrast.title: Contrasting
flightPlan.help.discover.details: Automatic cask/age settings add 5 × weighted coverage of untasted cask families Knew, up to 1 point for differences from the closest known subtypes in history (4 × Jnew), and 3 per untasted age class Qnew. Comparison uses the entire recorded tasting history.
flightPlan.help.discover.text: Favors untasted or long-unvisited bottlings. Rarely tasted cask families and age classes are new discovery signals; unfamiliar radar profiles remain optional.
flightPlan.help.discover.title: Discover
flightPlan.help.families: Dominant aroma families: smoke/peat/medicinal, fruit/floral, wood/cereal, wine, and feinty/sulphury. Each family takes the highest assessed axis. It qualifies from a score of 2 upwards. A bottling has at most one dominant family.
flightPlan.help.intro: Suggestions are calculated locally using deterministic rules and your collection data. No flavors are invented, and no AI or external services are used.
flightPlan.help.limitationsDetails: The formulas are interpretable heuristics, not scientifically validated sensory scores. Free-text cask information may be partially or incorrectly classified. Missing facts are not fabricated. Plans remain manually editable.
flightPlan.help.limits: Uses recorded radar values, history, cask descriptions, age, bottle status, distilleries and alcohol strength. Neither the 0–100 rating nor price influences selection. Suggestions can be edited manually.
flightPlan.help.limits.title: Limitations and manual adjustments
flightPlan.help.order: Estimated intensity combines alcohol percentage, mean recorded profile intensity and additional smoke/peat contributions. For up to six bottles, all possible orders are compared. The algorithm prefers a gentle start, moderate intensity steps and neighboring whiskies with compatible profiles, and penalizes intensity reversals and harsh transitions. It is a heuristic, not a proven sensory assessment.
flightPlan.help.profileData: The ten radar axes contain scores from 0 to 10. A recorded 0 is a valid assessment; an empty value is unknown. The latest available flavor profile is used, which need not belong to the latest tasting.
flightPlan.help.search.improve: Optimization: up to two passes replace individual bottles with better alternatives. Ties are resolved deterministically; global optimality is not guaranteed.
flightPlan.help.search.seeds: Multiple seeds: the six highest-ranked bottles and one representative of each known aroma and cask family. Each subsequent choice maximizes the score of the whole current set.
flightPlan.help.search.shortlist: Shortlist: 48 strong individual candidates, up to eight per aroma family, six per cask family, four per age class, plus flavor extremes for Balanced/Contrast.
flightPlan.help.search.title: How the set is assembled
flightPlan.help.sequenceDetails: Delta is the change in intensity from A to B. Added to the existing transition costs are 0.65 × cask distance when known and 0.025 × min(age gap, 15) when both ages are known. Age influence is deliberately small. All n! sequences are scored for up to six bottles (720 maximum).
flightPlan.help.sequenceIntro: After selecting the set, every sequence of up to six bottles is evaluated by intensity, flavor, cask and small age transition costs.
flightPlan.help.similar.details: Each comparable pair contributes 3.2 times the signed combined distance. The default direction is −1. An explicit varied casks/ages preference reverses only that component. Pairs with fewer than two shared rated radar axes still incur −14.
flightPlan.help.similar.text: Minimizes weighted pairwise distances for flavor (65%), cask type (25%) and age (10%). Flavor focus and additional cask/age preferences are supported.
flightPlan.help.similar.title: Similar flavors
flightPlan.help.strategies.intro: S scores the entire selected group; higher scores win. All strategies subtract 2 per repeated distillery. Automatic cask/age contributions and any user preferences (Pref) are added.

J: mean subtype contribution across all pairs; Jnew: mean closest comparable subtype contribution per bottle against history; missing contributions are zero.

flightPlan.help.vars.distanceSum: Sum of signed, weighted combined pairwise distances (Dsigned), using only known components.

flightPlan.help.vars.gap: Largest gap between estimated intensities sorted in ascending order.
flightPlan.help.vars.missing: Number of bottle pairs with fewer than two commonly assessed radar axes.
flightPlan.help.vars.other: Per-bottle novelty and minimum distance to other historical profiles, as defined above.
flightPlan.help.vars.profiled: Number of bottles with at least two assessed radar axes.
flightPlan.help.vars.repeats: Number of selected bottlings whose distillery has already appeared in the set.
flightPlan.help.vars.score: Total score of the entire selected set; higher is better.

help.analysis.1: Reports use stored data without estimating missing values. Some reports require valid dates or purchase prices.
help.analysis.2: For bottlings with multiple distilleries, a bottle may be attributed to each distillery. Costs in different currencies are not automatically converted.
help.analysis.title: Analytics
help.backups.1: Use a password-protected full ZIP backup to preserve the collection, storage, images and documents.
help.backups.2: A simple JSON export from Settings is not a full backup: pictures, documents and storage assignments may be missing.
help.backups.3: Scheduled backups may target USB, NAS or cloud storage. Store the password separately and keep backups safe.
help.backups.4: Offline release packages archive dependencies and AI files for rebuilding; archived Docker images can run without package servers. Test recovery ahead of time.
help.backups.title: Backups and recovery
help.basics.1: Create a bottling first, then add its individual physical bottles or samples.
help.basics.2: Search and filter bottlings or individual bottles in the collection, and switch between cards and table.
help.basics.3: A bottling describes the product. Each physical bottle may have its own inventory number, condition and photos.
help.basics.4: The menu links to Collection, Tasting notes, Analytics, Storage, Map, Settings and this Help page.
help.basics.title: Getting started
help.bottlings.1: For blends, select multiple contributing distilleries only when their involvement is known. Do not guess unknown components.
help.bottlings.2: Origin is derived from assigned distilleries. Bottlings with multiple distilleries can have more than one country of origin.
help.bottlings.3: Select “Composition complete” only when all components are known. Unknown information may be left blank.
help.bottlings.4: Add distilleries while editing a bottling or in Settings. Locations appear on the map when coordinates are available.
help.bottlings.5: Colour, flavour profile, notes and score are recorded per tasting. A bottling can have any number of dated tastings. Missing profile values are not the same as zero.
help.bottlings.6: Bottling details show the latest tasting and its score. Use “New tasting” or “All tasting notes” to create a tasting or open the history; bottling information remains separate.
help.bottlings.7: Use the arrow beside “Edit” in the bottling details to change the completion status directly. Opening the menu changes nothing; only selecting the action saves the status. You can undo the change for a short time afterwards.
help.bottlings.title: Bottlings and distilleries
help.data.1: The collection uses data/collection.json; rooms and shelf assignments use data/warehouse.json. These are server-managed files, not browser storage.
help.data.2: Photos and documents are stored separately in the persistent data directory. On Raspberry Pi the directory is outside the Git checkout and container.
help.data.3: Updating application code or Docker images must not overwrite persistent data. Make a full backup before upgrades.
help.data.4: Language and light/dark mode are configurable. The optional founding year appears on the collection overview; leaving it blank hides it.
help.data.title: Data storage and settings
help.description: Find guides for bottlings, tasting notes, tasting flights, storage, maps, photos, analytics, backups and data storage.
help.flights.1: Under “Tasting notes”, use “Create flight” to create a session with a name, date and optional shared notes.
help.flights.2: Add existing tasting notes or create new tastings for owned or other bottlings within the flight. A tasting note can belong to at most one flight.
help.flights.3: Reorder tastings by dragging their handle with a mouse or touch, or use the Up/Down buttons. The order is saved without changing individual scores.
help.flights.4: “Remove” detaches a tasting from the flight without deleting the note. Deleting the entire flight also leaves its individual tasting notes intact.
help.flights.5: If an external tasting is later assigned to a collected bottling, its flight position is preserved. The order records the sequence but does not calculate any effect on the score.
help.flights.title: Tasting flights
help.guide.backups.dropbox.1: On the Pi from the project directory run docker compose exec app rclone config. Choose “n” to add a remote, give it a name such as dropbox-wcm and choose the Dropbox storage type.
help.guide.backups.dropbox.2: Follow the OAuth prompts. On a headless Pi use the authorization flow Rclone offers for another computer. Do not paste credentials into application notes.
help.guide.backups.dropbox.3: Verify the connection with docker compose exec app rclone lsd dropbox-wcm:. In backup administration enter the remote name dropbox-wcm and a subfolder, run a manual backup and verify the destination.
help.guide.backups.dropbox.title: Set up Dropbox (Rclone)
help.guide.backups.manual.1: Choose “Download protected backup” and save the ZIP outside the Raspberry Pi. A JSON-only export is not a full backup.
help.guide.backups.manual.2: Open the ZIP with 7-Zip and the central password. Check data/, images/ and documents/. The data folder contains collection.json and warehouse.json.
help.guide.backups.manual.3: Note: file names in the encrypted ZIP remain visible. ZIP32 archives are limited to just under 4 GiB.
help.guide.backups.manual.title: Test the first backup
help.guide.backups.nas.1: Mount the NAS on the Raspberry Pi host under ${WCM_DATA_DIR}/backup-targets/<name>. The application container does not need mount privileges.
help.guide.backups.nas.2: Before creating the .whisky-backup-target marker, verify the share is actually mounted and writable. Create a local backup profile for the proper subfolder.
help.guide.backups.nas.3: For regular use configure a reliable systemd mount or /etc/fstab entry on the host. Check connectivity and test writes after reboots.
help.guide.backups.nas.title: NAS and network shares
help.guide.backups.onedrive.1: Run docker compose exec app rclone config, choose “n”, name the remote onedrive-wcm and select the OneDrive storage provider.
help.guide.backups.onedrive.2: Authorize your Microsoft account and select the drive type and drive. On a headless Pi use Rclone’s instructions for authentication on another computer.
help.guide.backups.onedrive.3: Test with docker compose exec app rclone lsd onedrive-wcm:. In the cloud backup profile specify the remote name and destination path; create a test backup and open it with the ZIP password.
help.guide.backups.onedrive.title: Set up OneDrive (Rclone)
help.guide.backups.other.1: Google Drive, SFTP, S3 and WebDAV also use Rclone. Setup is provider-specific; select the appropriate storage type in rclone config and verify the remote with rclone lsd.
help.guide.backups.other.2: Rclone configuration is persisted in ${WCM_DATA_DIR}/rclone/rclone.conf. Do not copy credentials or tokens into public documents.
help.guide.backups.other.title: Other cloud destinations
help.guide.backups.restore.1: Under “Restore backup” select the ZIP and enter that archive’s password. The application validates it in a protected staging area and shows a preview without changing the live collection.
help.guide.backups.restore.2: Only after confirmation are data, images and documents restored. An additional encrypted safety ZIP is created first; ensure sufficient free storage for staging.
help.guide.backups.restore.3: Old Restic backups require their separate legacy Restic key. Convert those backups to ZIP via the legacy import flow first.
help.guide.backups.restore.4: A complete rebuild requires both the data ZIP and a separately archived offline release with container images and AI assets. See docs/OFFLINE_RELEASES.md.
help.guide.backups.restore.title: Restore and disaster recovery
help.guide.backups.schedule.1: Each destination can back up hourly, daily or weekly. The application manages daily, weekly and monthly retention per destination.
help.guide.backups.schedule.2: After the first backup check its status and the available snapshots. Use test/check jobs; ZIPs are verified, including AES-HMAC, before publication.
help.guide.backups.schedule.3: The backup worker runs independently of the browser. For failures examine target mounts, Rclone remotes, free space, admin credentials and backup worker logs.
help.guide.backups.schedule.title: Schedules, retention and logs
help.guide.backups.setup.1: After the Pi setup, open Settings → Backups. Unlock with the backup administrator token stored in ${WCM_DATA_DIR}/secrets/backup-admin-token.
help.guide.backups.setup.2: Set the central ZIP password (at least 14 characters) and confirm it. It is stored in ${WCM_DATA_DIR}/backup-control/backup-zip-password. Keep a separate copy securely off the Raspberry Pi.
help.guide.backups.setup.3: This one password protects manual downloads and scheduled USB, NAS and cloud ZIP files (AES-256 WinZip AE-2). You need the relevant password to restore an archive.
help.guide.backups.setup.4: The admin token unlocks backup administration; Rclone credentials authenticate cloud services. Neither is the ZIP password. If you change the ZIP password, keep old passwords for older archives.
help.guide.backups.setup.title: Initial setup and central password
help.guide.backups.usb.1: Connect the stick to the Raspberry Pi. From the project folder run sh deploy/setup-usb.sh and select the UUID of the actual attached drive. The script does not format the stick.
help.guide.backups.usb.2: The mount is temporary and does not add an /etc/fstab entry. Remount after reboot, or configure a persistent mount yourself.
help.guide.backups.usb.3: Unlock backup administration → “Configure backup destination” → “USB stick”. Disable the schedule for the initial test, save, run “Back up now” and “Show backups”.
help.guide.backups.usb.4: Verify the .whisky-backup-target marker on the actually mounted drive. This guards against silently writing to the SD card when the stick is missing.
help.guide.backups.usb.title: USB stick as backup destination
help.intro: Guides and answers for Whisky Collection Manager.
help.map.1: “All distilleries” also displays sites without any bottles. Switching preserves the map center and zoom.
help.map.2: Zoom with the mouse wheel, plus/minus controls or touch gestures. “Show all locations” deliberately refits the viewport.
help.map.3: Selecting a distillery focuses it. Map tiles come from OpenStreetMap and need internet access; collection data stays local.
help.map.title: Map
help.photos.1: Photos can be associated with individual bottles and bottlings. A placeholder is shown when there is no photo.
help.photos.2: The photo editor supports adjustments and optional bottle cutout using the locally provided AI model.
help.photos.3: Originals are retained. Check cutout edges before saving, particularly on glass and transparent areas.
help.photos.title: Photos and cutouts
help.storage.1: Create rooms and furniture in the floor plan. Move and position furniture in 2D; inspect visibility and orientation in 3D. Double-click an occupied 3D shelf to view its contents.
help.storage.2: In “Shelves & Compartments”, click a bottle to select it for bulk actions; double-click a bottle to open its brief details. Double-click a compartment surface to see all bottles.
help.storage.3: Use the furniture edit icon to manage its compartments. Clicking a bottle inside the furniture/compartment editor opens its brief details; closing returns to the previous dialog.
help.storage.4: Bottle images in the shelf contents dialog are not selectable. Use “Relocate” or “Go to details”. Empty 3D compartments do not open a contents dialog.
help.storage.5: Compartments can have fixed/automatic heights and capacities (0 means unavailable). When deleting a room with bottles, cancel or unassign its bottles before deleting it.
help.storage.6: Use “Shelves & bays” to edit furniture and shelves. In a shelf editor switch with Previous/Next; save or discard unsaved changes, or cancel navigation.
help.storage.7: Multiple photos are stored on the furniture as a whole. Copies do not inherit photos. Full ZIP backups include files; collection-only JSON exports do not.
help.storage.title: Rooms, furniture and shelves
help.tastings.1: Open “Tasting notes” from the menu. Select “New tasting” to choose a bottling from your collection, or “Other bottling” for a whisky you do not own.
help.tastings.2: For a collected bottling, you can also create a tasting or open “All tasting notes” from the bottling details. Each bottling supports any number of independent tastings.
help.tastings.3: Every tasting needs a date. A title is optional; record impressions separately for nose, palate and finish.
help.tastings.4: Optionally select the whisky colour and set the ten flavour-profile axes from 0 to 10. Colour, flavour profile and overall score can each be cleared.
help.tastings.5: The overall score ranges from 0 to 100 points. Five proportionally filled Glencairn glasses show the rating, with 20 points per glass. An optional comment can accompany the rating.
help.tastings.6: Saved tastings initially open in read-only mode. Choose “Edit” to change the fields and “Done” to return to the view. Newly created tastings open directly in edit mode.
help.tastings.7: The latest tasting by tasting date determines the score shown in bottling details and on the collection card. The collection has a rating-range quick filter. If the latest tasting has no score, an older score is not substituted.
help.tastings.8: With “Other bottling”, the bottling information belongs only to this tasting; no inventory entry is created. If you later buy it, use “Assign bottling” to attach the tasting to an existing collection bottling while preserving notes and score.
help.tastings.title: Tasting notes

warehouse.wall.instructions: Double-click a compartment to view all its bottles. Tap or click bottles to highlight them (tap again to deselect). Drag highlighted bottles together to another compartment or use Assign. Cabinet positions follow the room layout; stacked furniture remains stacked. For one highlighted bottle, use Bottle details to open its individual preview with relocate and detail-page actions.

warehouse.wall.scrollAria: Scroll horizontally through the shelf wall
warehouse.wall.unassignedEmpty: All bottles are assigned to a compartment.
warehouse.wall.unassignedSearchPlacehold: Search bottle name or inventory number
warehouse.walls.description: Switch each panel on or off independently of the doors.
warehouse.walls.glassDoorFrameDefault: Glass door frame (default for all compartments)
insurance.title: Insurance documentation
insurance.description: Inventory and purchase evidence for the current whisky stock.
insurance.scope: Current stock excluding empty bottles; samples are optional. General analytics filters do not apply here.
insurance.evidenceNote: Only personal photos and explicitly designated purchase evidence count; Whiskybase images and other attachments are not purchase or ownership evidence. The checklist concerns recorded details, not their authenticity or acceptance by insurers. Acquisition costs are not replacement values.
insurance.exportNote: The ZIP includes the detailed report, personal original photos, all linked attachments and a manifest. Exports are unencrypted and may contain sensitive data. The package is built in the browser (maximum 2 GiB). It does not replace a backup.
insurance.exportFailed: The export could not be completed. Check media availability and package size.
